title: Portable Local Staging and Hostinger Production Separation

phases.objective: Provide a portable Windows/External SSD Staging topology with three dedicated MariaDB bindings, an opt-in Dev-only Cloudflare Tunnel, Hostinger Cloud production separation, and fail-closed mutation defaults.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The repository proves the three local database services, SSD bind mounts, disabled-by-default mutation flags, optional Dev-only tunnel profile, and Hostinger deployment boundary without starting a database, applying SQL, reading credentials, or mutating Production.
steps: Parse the staging Compose and environment templates without starting containers.
Verify runtime, governance, and persistence databases have distinct services, identities, names, and SSD bind mounts.
Verify the app depends on healthy local database services and the staging safety flags remain false.
Verify the Cloudflare service is opt-in behind the tunnel profile and targets the local app network rather than a Production hostname or credential.
Verify the Hostinger deployment documentation keeps Production on the Production branch and treats Redis as disabled or externally managed on Cloud hosting.
Run the bounded topology regression and emit only secret-free pass/fail evidence.
assertions: The three database bindings are not conflated: DB_*, GOVERNANCE_DB_*, and RUNTIME_PERSISTENCE_DB_* remain separate.
MIGRATION_APPLIED=false and DATABASE_MUTATED=false remain explicit defaults, and no migration or SQL apply is executed.
The Cloudflare Tunnel service is not part of the default startup path and uses only a Dev token supplied through the untracked staging environment.
Production remains on Hostinger Cloud and never reuses the Dev tunnel hostname, token, DNS record, or External SSD state.
Hostinger Cloud operation without Redis is represented as disabled queue mode; queued Production operation requires a separate external managed Redis endpoint.
No provider mutation, credential output, deployment promotion, main mutation, or Production mutation is introduced by this change.

phases.objective: Expose Dev through a manually provisioned Cloudflare Tunnel and validate the local app externally without reusing Production credentials or authorizing SQL mutation.
blockers: A dedicated Cloudflare Dev tunnel and dev.mad4b.com ingress must be provisioned by an authorized operator.
The Dev tunnel token is not present in the repository and must remain in the untracked local environment.
External route validation requires a running Windows/WSL2 Docker host and is not performed in repository CI.

phases.objective: Preserve portability and fail-closed behavior across Windows machines and External SSD reconnection without sharing state with Hostinger Production.
No external provider canary or DNS mutation is introduced by this repository change.
Production remains a separately governed Hostinger release requiring exact Production promotion, Hostinger runtime readback, database capability verification, and explicit Redis/provider readiness.
blockers: No Hostinger deployment or Production promotion is authorized by this source PR.
No Production database migration, grant, or SQL apply is authorized.
Production secrets and any external Redis credential must be configured only in the Hostinger environment and never committed.
